title: The bassoon in his arrangements, and comedians burlesquing it
summary: A guitarist doubled bassoon and Randolph used it extensively; he resents radio comedy turning a beautiful instrument into a clown.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: That bassoon fascinates me. Did you use it on anything exceptional at the time?
The bassoon, the guitar player who doubled the bassoon.
Well, yes, I used it quite a bit, you

see. I'm trying to think, what arrangement did I use the bassoon in. And this boy was very good with that bassoon. The bassoon is pretty. That's why -- I was telling my wife, you know, sometimes a comedy will come along on the radio, and they'd have the bassoon (musical sounds).

I told my wife, I said, you know, now, that's a disgrace. I told her, now, that's naturally really -- the people are trying to make a clown out of that instrument, and that instrument is beautiful when it's used right.
It really is. You know, I'll tell you, Mr. DiMichael, I am so wrapped up in music til it really bugs me when somebody tries to burlesque it. Doesn't it bug you?
When they try to -- I mean real music, when they try to burlesque the music.

It's all right if they're going to take a comedy and got a comedy skit. But if they're going to take a -- now, you take a beautiful thing like an instrument as a bassoon, and you'll never hear -- I don't know what's the matter with them -- you'll never hear a bassoon going no time
Or something else happening, and then they got to take the bassoon and here they go, and the guy that's playing it, he's not trying to get no beauty out of it, he's trying to (musical sounds).
